title: 葛生
author: 佚名（《诗经·唐风》）
authorEn: Anonymous (Book of Songs, Airs of Tang)
intro: Vines creep over a grave; the woman who visits it asks, “Who is with me now? No one.” Often called the earliest Chinese poem of mourning for a husband or wife, it ends with a quiet promise: after a hundred years, I will lie beside you.
analysis: 这首诗一般被认为是中国最早的“悼亡诗”——为死去的丈夫或妻子写的诗。开头写坟地的景象：葛藤爬满了荆棘，蔹草蔓延在田野和墓地上，一片荒凉。“予美亡此”——我心爱的人不在了，长眠在这里。“谁与？独处！”自问自答，只有三个字，却写尽了孤单。第三章写到家里那只角枕、那床锦被还是那样鲜亮，人却已经不在，只能独自熬到天亮——用旧物写思念，最让人心酸。最后两章，“夏之日，冬之夜”，夏天的白天最长，冬天的夜晚最长，日子漫长难熬；两章把“日”和“夜”调换顺序，好像一年又一年地重复。结尾的心愿很平静：等我百年之后，就到你那里去，和你葬在一起。今天中国人说“百年之后”，就是对“去世”的委婉说法。
analysisEn: This is often called the earliest Chinese poem of mourning for a husband or wife (悼亡诗). It begins at a grave: kudzu vines smother the thorn bushes, bindweed creeps across the fields and the burial ground. 予美亡此 — “the one I love is gone, and lies here.” Then three tiny words, a question and its answer: 谁与？独处！ — “Who is with me? I am alone.” In the third stanza we are back in the house: the pillow inlaid with horn and the brocade quilt still look bright and new, but the person who shared them is gone, and she lies awake alone until dawn. Old belongings bringing back the dead is one of the most moving moves in Chinese poetry. The last two stanzas say 夏之日，冬之夜 — summer days are the longest days, winter nights the longest nights — so time drags endlessly; swapping “day” and “night” in the final stanza makes it feel like year after year going round. The ending is calm: after my hundred years, I will come to your resting place and lie beside you. Chinese still says 百年之后, “after a hundred years”, as a gentle way of saying “after I die”.
background: The Book of Songs gathers 305 songs from roughly the 11th to the 6th century BC. This one is from the “Airs of Tang” (唐风), the state of Jin in present-day Shanxi. Traditional commentators linked it to the long wars of Jin; the speaker is usually read as a widow.
pronunciation: 予 yú（我）；谁与 shuí yǔ；独处 chǔ；蔹 liǎn；蔓 màn；角枕 jiǎo zhěn；粲 càn；衾 qīn；域 yù。“谁”按古诗习惯注 shuí，口语读 shéi 亦可。
version: 采用通行的《毛诗》文本，全诗五章，每章四句，网站按意思排成每章两行。

lines.py: gé shēng méng chǔ, liǎn màn yú yě
lines.lit: The kudzu grows, covering the thorn bushes; the bindweed spreads over the wild fields.
lines.en: Kudzu climbs over the thorn bushes, bindweed creeps across the fields.

lines.py: yú měi wáng cǐ, shuí yǔ, dú chǔ
lines.lit: My beloved is gone from here — who is with me? I stay alone!
lines.en: The one I love is gone and lies here. Who keeps me company? No one — I live alone.

lines.py: gé shēng méng jí, liǎn màn yú yù
lines.lit: The kudzu grows, covering the jujube thorns; the bindweed spreads over the graveyard.
lines.en: Kudzu climbs over the thorns, bindweed creeps across the graves.

lines.py: yú měi wáng cǐ, shuí yǔ, dú xī
lines.lit: My beloved is gone from here — who is with me? I rest alone!
lines.en: The one I love is gone and lies here. Who keeps me company? No one — I lie down alone.

lines.py: jiǎo zhěn càn xī, jǐn qīn làn xī
lines.lit: The horn-inlaid pillow is bright; the brocade quilt is shining.
lines.en: The pillow inlaid with horn still gleams, the brocade quilt still glows.

lines.py: yú měi wáng cǐ, shuí yǔ, dú dàn
lines.lit: My beloved is gone from here — who is with me? Alone until dawn!
lines.en: The one I love is gone and lies here. Who keeps me company? No one — I wait alone for the dawn.

lines.py: xià zhī rì, dōng zhī yè
lines.en: Long summer days, long winter nights —

lines.py: bǎi suì zhī hòu, guī yú qí jū
lines.lit: After a hundred years, I will return to his dwelling.
lines.en: when my hundred years are done, I will go home to where he lies.

lines.py: dōng zhī yè, xià zhī rì
lines.en: Long winter nights, long summer days —

lines.py: bǎi suì zhī hòu, guī yú qí shì
lines.lit: After a hundred years, I will return to his chamber.
lines.en: when my hundred years are done, I will join him in his room.

words.note: 一种爬藤植物，古人用它的纤维织布。
古义指荆条；今天多指楚国、湖北一带。
亡：不在、死去，现代汉语“死亡”。
古义指墓地；今天“区域”“领域”指范围。
现代汉语“元旦”“通宵达旦”。

words.en: after (my) hundred years — after I die
words.note: 今天说“百年之后”，是“去世”的委婉说法。

imagery.name: 葛
imagery.zh: 葛藤爬满坟地，写出墓地的荒凉；藤蔓缠绕依附，也像她对亡夫的牵挂缠绕不去。
imagery.en: Kudzu smothering the graves shows how desolate the place is; the clinging vine is also like her love, still wrapped around the man she lost.
